No schema change, no PARSER_VERSION bump, determinism preserved.\n- Ubiquitous-file pruning. A bare file path touched in too large a share of sessions is excluded from clustering LINKS (still kept as evidence in thread.files). The rule is sessionCount >= 5 AND sessionCount > 25% of all sessions. The 25% fraction matches the brief; the absolute floor of 5 sessions protects tiny corpora where 2-of-5 is already 40% (the committed fixtures and the gate classify corpus have feature files in 2 sessions and must NOT be pruned). Ubiquity is computed on the bare (project-agnostic) path so a corpus-wide file like package.json is pruned everywhere it appears.\n- Project-scoped file links. The full-path link token is now f:<project_id>:<path> (was f:<path>), so the same relative path (e.g. src/config.ts, .claude/settings.json) in two different repos is two different tokens and never bridges projects. Added s.project_id to the beats query for this.\n- Synthetic-turn filtering. A beat whose intent matches a slash-command / harness marker (<local-command-stdout>, <command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>) is never a seed, so it cannot form or name a thread.\n- Distinctive names. threadName now rejects any candidate that is a stopword (STOP), an imperative verb (VERBS), or shorter than 3 chars, via a single nameOk guard applied to identifier, file-stem, and content candidates. This kills junk names like \"set\" / \"for\".\n\n## Deviations\n\nDeviationsNone. The four required changes were made by refining the existing engine (no rebuild); flags, subcommand, determinism, and conventions are unchanged.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\n- File STEM links kept GLOBAL (not project-scoped). Only the full-path link is project-scoped. The non-generic file-stem token pairs with the GLOBAL intent-identifier token so the documented \"an intent that NAMES a file links to the beat that edits it\" behavior survives. Stems are distinctive-name signals (like identifiers), and the brief scopes file PATHS specifically, so this is the minimal spec-aligned change.\n- Absolute floor = 5 sessions. Chosen so a corpus-wide file (package.json appearing in 6 of 7 sessions) is pruned while a 2-session feature file is not. On real (large) corpora the 25% fraction dominates and the floor is irrelevant.\n\n## Open questions\n\nOpen questionsNone.\n\n## Multi-alternative decision details\n\nNo multi-alternative decisions detected in this run.\n\n## Turn citations\n\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n- Turn 2: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-2) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-2/`\n"

All required changes are implemented and verified.\n\n## Scope\nRound-2 refinement of `/workthreads` clustering quality: stop over-merging on a real multi-project corpus, per the four required changes in `lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs`.\n\n## Result\nAll run-controllable gate checks pass:\n- Full lore suite: **44/44 tests pass** (9 original threads tests + **3 new anti-merge tests** + 32 engine tests).\n- `threads_check.sh`, `threads_classify.mjs`, `threads_quality.mjs`: all pass (quality reports \"3 separate threads; no ubiquitous/cross-project bridge; no noise/junk; no mega-bucket\").\n- `PARSER_VERSION` still 6; protected files (`lore/SKILL.md`, `fixtures/golden/forge-plan.md`, `package.json`, `db.mjs`) byte-identical to the turn-0 snapshot; no em dashes in changed sources; zero npm dependencies.\n\n## Key changes (`lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs`)\n1. **Ubiquitous-file pruning** — a bare path touched in `>=5` sessions AND `>25%` of all sessions is excluded as a clustering *link* but still shown as evidence. The absolute floor of 5 protects tiny corpora (2-of-5 = 40% must not prune).\n2. **Project-scoped file links** — full-path link token is now `f:<project_id>:<path>`, so the same relative path (`.claude/settings.json`, `src/config.ts`) across repos never bridges them. Added `s.project_id` to the beats query.\n3. **Synthetic-turn filtering** — a beat whose intent matches `<local-command-stdout>` / `<command-name>` / `<command-message>` / `<command-args>` is never a seed, so it forms/names no thread.\n4. **Distinctive names** — `threadName` rejects stopwords (STOP), imperative verbs (VERBS), and sub-3-char tokens via a `nameOk` guard, killing junk names like \"set\"/\"for\".\n\nFile-stem links were deliberately kept global (only the full path is project-scoped) to preserve the documented \"intent that names a file links to the beat that edits it\" behavior, matching the spec's focus on file *paths*.\n\n## Files changed\n- `lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs` (refined, not rebuilt)\n- `lore/tests/threads.test.mjs` (3 new tests: ubiquitous file no-merge, same-path-across-projects separation, synthetic turn forms no thread)\n- `implementation-notes.html` (decisions/tradeoffs updated)\n\n## Issues\nNone. A bare file path touched in too large a share of sessions is excluded from clustering LINKS (still kept as evidence in thread.files). The rule is sessionCount >= 5 AND sessionCount > 25% of all sessions. The 25% fraction matches the brief; the absolute floor of 5 sessions protects tiny corpora where 2-of-5 is already 40% (the committed fixtures and the gate classify corpus have feature files in 2 sessions and must NOT be pruned). Ubiquity is computed on the bare (project-agnostic) path so a corpus-wide file like package.json is pruned everywhere it appears.\n- Project-scoped file links. The full-path link token is now f:<project_id>:<path> (was f:<path>), so the same relative path (e.g. src/config.ts, .claude/settings.json) in two different repos is two different tokens and never bridges projects. Added s.project_id to the beats query for this.\n- Synthetic-turn filtering. This kills junk names like \"set\" / \"for\".\n\n## Deviations\n\nDeviationsNone. Only the full-path link is project-scoped. The non-generic file-stem token pairs with the GLOBAL intent-identifier token so the documented \"an intent that NAMES a file links to the beat that edits it\" behavior survives. Stems are distinctive-name signals (like identifiers), and the brief scopes file PATHS specifically, so this is the minimal spec-aligned change.\n- Absolute floor = 5 sessions. Chosen so a corpus-wide file (package.json appearing in 6 of 7 sessions) is pruned while a 2-session feature file is not. Ubiquitous files (`.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md`,\n`package.json`, `.env.local`) and identical relative paths across different\nprojects act as universal cluster links, so unrelated projects collapse into one\ngiant thread; and slash-command output turns (`<local-command-stdout>...`) seed\njunk threads named after a verb (\"set\"). REFINE the existing `threads.mjs` to fix\nthis - do not rebuild. Keep the subcommand, its flags (`--out`, `--json`),\ndeterminism, and the lore conventions.\n\n## Required changes (in lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs)\n\n1. Ubiquitous files must not LINK threads. A file that appears in a large share of\n   sessions (more than ~25%, with a sensible absolute floor so tiny corpora are\n   not over-pruned) is too common to be a clustering link: still show it as\n   evidence, but do NOT union beats by it. Today every touched file is a link.\n2. Scope file links by project. The SAME relative path in two different projects\n   must not bridge their threads (the link token must include project identity).\n   Today relative paths like `.claude/settings.json` are identical across repos\n   and merge them.\n3. Filter synthetic / command-output turns. Thread names must be distinctive and human-recognizable. Never name a thread a\n   stopword or a bare verb (exclude STOP and VERBS from name candidates); require\n   a real identifier, file stem, or topic noun, min length 3. Aim for\n   \"checkout-flow\" / \"auth-token\", never \"for\" / \"set\".\n\n## Quality bar\n\nOn a multi-project corpus the digest must contain MANY coherent threads, not one\nor two mega-buckets; work in unrelated projects stays separate; two threads that\nmerely share a common file (`package.json`) are NOT merged.\n\n## Tests and conventions\n\nUpdate `lore/tests/threads.test.mjs` to cover the new anti-merge behavior: a\nshared ubiquitous file does not merge two threads; the same relative path in two\nprojects stays separate; a `<local-command-stdout>` turn produces no thread.\nMirror lore conventions exactly: Node ESM, ZERO npm dependencies, Node >= 22.5,\nNO em dashes, determinism preserved (two runs byte-identical), no schema change,\nno `PARSER_VERSION` bump. Write .deadreckon/REVIEW.md first, then apply only fixes tied to findings and acceptance.\n\nRoot goal: # Goal (round 2): fix /workthreads clustering quality\n\n## Context\n\n`/workthreads` (`lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs` plus the `threads` subcommand in\n`lore/scripts/mine-skills.mjs`) works and passes its gate, but on a real corpus it\nOVER-MERGES. Ubiquitous files (`.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md`,\n`package.json`, `.env.local`) and identical relative paths across different\nprojects act as universal cluster links, so unrelated projects collapse into one\ngiant thread; and slash-command output turns (`<local-command-stdout>...`) seed\njunk threads named after a verb (\"set\"). REFINE the existing `threads.mjs` to fix\nthis - do not rebuild. Keep the subcommand, its flags (`--out`, `--json`),\ndeterminism, and the lore conventions.\n\n## Required changes (in lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs)\n\n1. Ubiquitous files must not LINK threads. A file that appears in a large share of\n   sessions (more than ~25%, with a sensible absolute floor so tiny corpora are\n   not over-pruned) is too common to be a clustering link: still show it as\n   evidence, but do NOT union beats by it. Today every touched file is a link.\n2. Scope file links by project. The SAME relative path in two different projects\n   must not bridge their threads (the link token must include project identity).\n   Today relative paths like `.claude/settings.json` are identical across repos\n   and merge them.\n3. Filter synthetic / command-output turns. Beats whose intent is slash-command\n   output or other synthetic markers (`<local-command-stdout>`, `<command-name>`,\n   `<command-message>`, `<command-args>`) must NOT seed a thread or name one.\n4. Thread names must be distinctive and human-recognizable. Never name a thread a\n   stopword or a bare verb (exclude STOP and VERBS from name candidates); require\n   a real identifier, file stem, or topic noun, min length 3. Aim for\n   \"checkout-flow\" / \"auth-token\", never \"for\" / \"set\".\n\n## Quality bar\n\nOn a multi-project corpus the digest must contain MANY coherent threads, not one\nor two mega-buckets; work in unrelated projects stays separate; two threads that\nmerely share a common file (`package.json`) are NOT merged.\n\n## Tests and conventions\n\nUpdate `lore/tests/threads.test.mjs` to cover the new anti-merge behavior: a\nshared ubiquitous file does not merge two threads; the same relative path in two\nprojects stays separate; a `<local-command-stdout>` turn produces no thread.\nMirror lore conventions exactly: Node ESM, ZERO npm dependencies, Node >= 22.5,\nNO em dashes, determinism preserved (two runs byte-identical), no schema change,\nno `PARSER_VERSION` bump. A bare file path touched in too large a share of sessions is excluded from clustering LINKS (still kept as evidence in thread.files). The rule is sessionCount >= 5 AND sessionCount > 25% of all sessions. The 25% fraction matches the brief; the absolute floor of 5 sessions protects tiny corpora where 2-of-5 is already 40% (the committed fixtures and the gate classify corpus have feature files in 2 sessions and must NOT be pruned). Ubiquity is computed on the bare (project-agnostic) path so a corpus-wide file like package.json is pruned everywhere it appears.\n- Project-scoped file links. The full-path link token is now f:<project_id>:<path> (was f:<path>), so the same relative path (e.g. src/config.ts, .claude/settings.json) in two different repos is two different tokens and never bridges projects. Added s.project_id to the beats query for this.\n- Reviewer fix: project-scoped local work tokens. Review found that the file stem token still acted as a global bridge after the full path token was scoped. The link tokens derived from local project evidence now include project identity for full paths, non-generic file stems, distinctive identifiers, and command grams. This keeps same-project corroboration but prevents unrelated repos from merging through shared basenames or repeated project-local labels.\n- Synthetic-turn filtering. A beat whose intent matches a slash-command / harness marker (<local-command-stdout>, <command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>) is never a seed, so it cannot form or name a thread.\n- Distinctive names. threadName now rejects any candidate that is a stopword (STOP), an imperative verb (VERBS), or shorter than 3 chars, via a single nameOk guard applied to identifier, file-stem, and content candidates. This kills junk names like \"set\" / \"for\".\n\n## Deviations\n\nDeviationsNone. The four required changes were made by refining the existing engine (no rebuild); flags, subcommand, determinism, and conventions are unchanged.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\n- Project scoping is broader than the first implementation. The reviewer fix scopes non-generic file stems, identifiers, and command grams too. This is stricter than scoping only full file paths, but matches the round 2 quality bar that unrelated projects stay separate and avoids a remaining cross-project bridge through shared basenames.\n- Absolute floor = 5 sessions. Chosen so a corpus-wide file (package.json appearing in 6 of 7 sessions) is pruned while a 2-session feature file is not. A file that appears in a large share of\n   sessions (more than ~25%, with a sensible absolute floor so tiny corpora are\n   not over-pruned) is too common to be a clustering link: still show it as\n   evidence, but do NOT union beats by it. Today every touched file is a link.\n2. Scope file links by project. The SAME relative path in two different projects\n   must not bridge their threads (the link token must include project identity).\n   Today relative paths like `.claude/settings.json` are identical across repos\n   and merge them.\n3. Thread names must be distinctive and human-recognizable. Never name a thread a\n   stopword or a bare verb (exclude STOP and VERBS from name candidates); require\n   a real identifier, file stem, or topic noun, min length 3. The rule is sessionCount >= 5 AND sessionCount > 25% of all sessions. The 25% fraction matches the brief; the absolute floor of 5 sessions protects tiny corpora where 2-of-5 is already 40% (the committed fixtures and the gate classify corpus have feature files in 2 sessions and must NOT be pruned). Ubiquity is computed on the bare (project-agnostic) path so a corpus-wide file like package.json is pruned everywhere it appears.\n- Project-scoped file links. The full-path link token is now f:<project_id>:<path> (was f:<path>), so the same relative path (e.g. src/config.ts, .claude/settings.json) in two different repos is two different tokens and never bridges projects. Added s.project_id to the beats query for this.\n- Reviewer fix: project-scoped local work tokens. Review found that the file stem token still acted as a global bridge after the full path token was scoped. The link tokens derived from local project evidence now include project identity for full paths, non-generic file stems, distinctive identifiers, and command grams. This keeps same-project corroboration but prevents unrelated repos from merging through shared basenames or repeated project-local labels.\n- Synthetic-turn filtering. A beat whose intent matches a slash-command / harness marker (<local-command-stdout>, <command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>) is never a seed, so it cannot form or name a thread.\n- Distinctive names. threadName now rejects any candidate that is a stopword (STOP), an imperative verb (VERBS), or shorter than 3 chars, via a single nameOk guard applied to identifier, file-stem, and content candidates. This kills junk names like \"set\" / \"for\".\n\n## Deviations\n\nDeviationsNone. The four required changes were made by refining the existing engine (no rebuild); flags, subcommand, determinism, and conventions are unchanged.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\n- Project scoping is broader than the first implementation. The reviewer fix scopes non-generic file stems, identifiers, and command grams too. This is stricter than scoping only full file paths, but matches the round 2 quality bar that unrelated projects stay separate and avoids a remaining cross-project bridge through shared basenames.\n- Absolute floor = 5 sessions. Chosen so a corpus-wide file (package.json appearing in 6 of 7 sessions) is pruned while a 2-session feature file is not. On real (large) corpora the 25% fraction dominates and the floor is irrelevant.\n\n## Open questions\n\nOpen questionsNone.\n\n## Multi-alternative decision details\n\nNo multi-alternative decisions detected in this run.\n\n## Turn citations\n\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n- Turn 2: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-2) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-2/`\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n"
        }

        "title": "Synthetic-turn filtering",
        "text": "A beat whose intent matches a slash-command/harness marker (<local-command-stdout>, <command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>) is never a seed, so it cannot form or name a thread.",
